Looking at the cuboid (5×2×2), the visible white cubes form a row of three along the top back edge. The only hidden cubes are the four along the bottom back edge.

- The light grey piece must take the hidden cube behind its bottom front cube (leftmost).
- The dark grey piece must take the hidden cube adjacent to its rightmost cube.
- That leaves the two middle hidden cubes for the white piece, directly beneath the middle and right cubes of its top row.

So the white piece is a flat shape: a row of three cubes with two cubes attached beneath the middle and end cubes — i.e., a 2×2 block with one extra cube attached (a "P" pentomino). Rotating this 90° gives two columns of heights 2 and 3 side by side, which matches diagram E.
